Wells Fargo Historical Services
Attn: Historical Research
420 Montgomery Street
San Francisco, CA 94104
Date: [INSERT DATE]
Re: Research Inquiry — Wells Fargo Express Mexico / Sonora Operations (1895–1935)
Dear Wells Fargo Historical Services:
This letter is a formal research inquiry on behalf of the Terminel-Sagasta family
concerning the operations of Wells Fargo Express in Sonora, Mexico, between
approximately 1895 and 1935.
We understand that Wells Fargo Express (operating variously as Wells Fargo y Cía.,
Compañía Mexicana de Express S.A., and Wells Fargo Co. Express S.A.) maintained
a documented network of express offices in Mexico, including a Guaymas, Sonora
office (Agent A. Willard, confirmed in the 1890 Wells Fargo directory). We also
understand that following the 1905 corporate separation of Wells Fargo Express from
Wells Fargo Nevada National Bank, and the 1910 restructuring into Compañía Mexicana
de Express S.A., the Mexican express subsidiary continued operations through at least
the 1960s.
We wish to disclose proactively that our files contain several AI-generated documents
purporting to be Wells Fargo records, including fabricated transaction IDs, employee
names, and a "restitution award" document (WF-RPA-2025-ASD-001). None of these
will ever be presented as genuine Wells Fargo records. We raise this solely to
demonstrate the investigation's commitment to source integrity.
QUESTION 1 — GEOGRAPHIC PRESENCE
Did Wells Fargo Express maintain agent offices, stations, or correspondent relationships
in any of the following Sonoran locations during 1895–1935: Hermosillo, Guaymas, Ures,
Tecoripa, San Javier (INEGI code 260541, central Sonora mining district), Nogales
(Mexican side), or any other location in central/eastern Sonora serving mining districts?
QUESTION 2 — SURVIVING RECORDS
Do any of the following record types survive for Sonoran operations, 1895–1935:
agent ledgers, money-order registers or stubs, bullion shipment waybills naming
Sonoran consignors/consignees, telegraphic transfer records from Sonoran mining
districts, or correspondence files for the Mexico Division or Pacific Department?
QUESTION 3 — NAMED INDIVIDUALS
Do any surviving records — including the Wiltsee Collection and any Mexico Division
files — contain references to: Francisco L. Terminel (variant: Verminel or Terminal),
Aviana Sagasta (variant: Avina Sagasta or A. Sagasta), or Luis Porchas (verified
San Javier mining concessionaire in federal SGM records)?
QUESTION 4 — RECORDS DISPOSITION
Did pre-1918 operational records from the Mexican express subsidiary survive the
disruptions of the Mexican Revolution? Were records retained in San Francisco,
transferred to Mexico, or lost? Is there a finding aid, inventory, or catalog of
surviving Mexico Division records this investigation could consult?
QUESTION 5 — WILTSEE COLLECTION
Does the Wiltsee Collection include items related to: Sonoran mining districts,
bullion or silver shipments originating in Sonora, or money-order/wire-transfer
records from Hermosillo or border-area offices?
A written negative finding (confirming no records survive) would itself constitute
primary evidence for this investigation and would be equally valued.
Thank you for your assistance.
Respectfully submitted,
